# Temple Scroll Column 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 17 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**17:1** The king must not take many wives, or they will lead his heart away from Me.

**17:2** He must not accumulate large amounts of silver and gold for himself.

**17:3** When he takes the throne of his kingdom, a copy of this law must be written for him

**17:4** on a scroll, taken from the one kept by the Levitical priests.

**17:5** He must keep it with him and read it every day of his life,

**17:6** so that he learns to revere Me and to carefully follow every word of this law

**17:7** and all these decrees.

**17:8** This will keep him from thinking he is better than his fellow Israelites or from straying from these commands in any way —

**17:9** so that he and his descendants may reign long over his kingdom in the midst of Israel.

**17:10** [blank line in manuscript]

**17:11** For the ordination, take one young bull and one ram from the flock,

**17:12** along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers coated with oil —

**17:13** all made from fine wheat flour.

**17:14** Place them in a single basket and bring them in the basket,

**17:15** along with the bull and the two rams.

**17:16** Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 17 transitions between two major topics. Lines 1-9 complete the Law of the King with its constraints on royal power — no polygamy, no excessive wealth, mandatory daily Scripture study. This vision of restrained monarchy is foundational to the Temple Scroll's theology. After a section break, lines 11-16 begin the priestly ordination instructions, closely paralleling Exodus 29:1-4. The juxtaposition implies that both king and priest serve under God's direct authority.*
